text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Neurology consultation in two weeks with nerve conduction studies to confirm or exclude a late post-frostbite neuropathy, entrapment, or another polyneuropathy, and to advise on treatment that does not cause drowsiness
  • Cold protection and hand care: liner gloves under mittens, heated gloves and hand warmers outdoors, warming the hands before fine work, no cold-water hand washing, and checking the fingers for skin damage
  • Blood tests for other causes of neuropathy: glucose and HbA1c, vitamin B12, TSH, kidney function, liver enzyme and hemoglobin; PHQ-9 for mood with chronic pain
  • Capsaicin 0.075% cream to the painful fingers four times a day for localized neuropathic pain, because he wishes to avoid oral treatment, with review in four weeks
  • Duloxetine 30 mg daily for a week, then 60 mg daily, for neuropathic pain not controlled by capsaicin cream, with review of pain, adverse effects, sleep, mood and blood pressure, a sodium check, no tramadol, and no abrupt stopping

resource.title: Roald Amundsen synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care and neurology for a 55-year-old polar explorer with cold-induced burning pain, numbness and color change in the fingers decades after frostbite: separating a late post-frostbite small-fiber neuropathy and cold-induced vasospasm from diabetes, B12 deficiency, thyroid disease and nerve entrapment with blood tests and nerve conduction studies; cold protection and hand care; pharmacological management by NICE CG173, choosing capsaicin cream first because he wishes to avoid tablets and then duloxetine, a first-line drug less sedating than amitriptyline or a gabapentinoid for a man who flies and drives; monitoring of pain, adverse effects, mood, sleep, blood pressure and sodium; avoiding tramadol with duloxetine; preventive care at 55; and a risk discussion about an Arctic air search flight: cold-water immersion, re-injury of previously frostbitten fingers, a stiff old shoulder fracture, and carrying and not stopping duloxetine. Built on NICE CG173, the Wilderness Medical Society frostbite (2024) and hypothermia (2019) guidelines, and the USPSTF and CDC preventive recommendations.
